items.title: For a locally finite type morphism the flat locus is open and there it is flat and locally of finite presentation, when the weakly associated points of the base are locally finite
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a morphism locally of finite type, the flat locus is an open subscheme on which the morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, under the hypothesis that the weakly associated points of the base are locally finite (statement lines 4179-4186). The proof reduces to the affine case and re-reads the finite type algebra map as a finite module over a polynomial algebra, after which the algebra form of the statement applies. The reduction and the change of variables are the substance, so the claim is H2.
